family: 0x?b  (byte0 low-nibble 0xb; byte0 HIGH nibble = destination register)
summary: The 0x?b group is TWO sub-families keyed on byte+2's LOW nibble: {0,1,9,b} = 4-byte COMPACT REGISTER MOVES (incl. the RAY-struct marshalling moves emitted around rt_intersect / intersection_query), and {7,e,f} = 10-byte source-modifier / logic / convert ALU forms. In every form byte0 HIGH nibble = destination register, byte+1 = source selector, byte+2 = source-class/op-form, byte+3 = operand type (0x08 = 32-bit register, 0x00 = none/zero). Closing the 4-byte marshalling moves (byte+2 0x40/0x41 + the 0x09 query-state move) removed the dominant root-desync cluster and cascade-closed downstream 0x00/0x54 debris.

descriptors.semantics: Float source-modifier / integer-logic move with an immediate/operand tail (10B). byte+2==0x0f selects the modifier-with-immediate form (vs 0x0e plain fmov, 0x1e/0x1f LUT2 logic). The op (fneg/fabs, or AND/OR with the trailing immediate) is chosen by byte+4/byte+5 exactly as in funary (byte+5: 0x00 mov,0x02 abs,0x0a neg) and ilogic; byte+6..9 carry the immediate/second operand. Op-select bits in the tail are INFERRED (shared with the HW-validated funary/ilogic), not independently splice-validated.

notes: byte0 HIGH nibble = destination register in EVERY 0x?b form (confirmed by the marshalling grids where dst high-nibble and src byte+1 vary INDEPENDENTLY, e.g. `bb 04 41 08 cb 06 41 08 db 08 41 08 ..`).

The 4-byte compact-move sub-family is ONE instruction shape: dst=byte0[4:8], src=byte+1, form=byte+2, opnd-type=byte+3. byte+2 bits6-7 look like a source-register-class selector (00=uniform bank uniform_mov, bit6=class-1 0x40/0x41, bit7=GPR/ray 0x80/0x81) and bit0=register-source-present -- this bit-level reading is INFERRED from byte+2/byte+3 co-variation, not splice-validated.

The RAY marshalling moves are NOT a new opcode: matrix TRANSPOSE (MPP) reuses the SAME 0x81/0x41 moves (round-1 finding); this round shows the copy form also has a bit6 variant (0x41) that dominates the ray-struct copy-in.

10-byte forms are distinguished purely by byte+2 low-nibble {7,e,f}; the exact op-select lives in the byte+4/byte+5 tail exactly as in the HW-validated funary/ilogic (byte+5: 0x00 mov, 0x02 abs, 0x0a neg). funary_imm (0x0f) and the b_alu10 fallbacks decode the length+operand frame but do NOT re-assert the tail op-select as independently validated.

Provenance is byte-diff / bracketing on OWN-MSL only (corpus + one freshly-compiled RT kernel). NO GPU dispatch was performed (shdump is compile-only; agxtest/agxrun were NOT run), so NOTHING here is claimed HW-VALIDATED. Field bit-packing is diff/bracket-inferred.

reg_move_c0/c1/c9/cb and b_alu10_lo7/loe/lof are FAMILY-LEVEL fallbacks (match on byte+2 low-nibble): they name+length+field-frame the many high-nibble source-class variants without asserting per-form semantics. Specific descriptors (ray_move_*, rtq_state_move, uniform_mov, tex_coord_setup, funary, ilogic) win by match specificity.
Multiple descriptors may NOT share a mnemonic in this DB (assemble/_BY_MNEM keeps only the last) -- each new descriptor was given a unique mnemonic so asm(disasm(b))==b holds.
